'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
**[[2024 Qala Bakhtiar bombing]]
***A [[Suicide attack|suicide bombing]] in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]], kills 6 people and injures 13. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-suicide-attack-kabul-97512251e817402114f07191dd3f230d (AP)]
*[[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]

**Hezbollah launches [[Katyusha rocket launcher|Katyusha rockets]] on [[Ein Ya'akov]], [[Ga'aton]] and [[Yehiam]], [[Northern District (Israel)|northern Israel]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/9/2/israeli-war-on-gaza-live-israel-bombs-school-killing-11-palestinians?update=3154128 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi militants]] strike two crude [[oil tanker]]s in the [[Red Sea]] with multiple missiles and [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/british-maritime-agencies-report-attacks-off-yemens-coast-2024-09-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Wreck of the Titanic|Wreck of the ''Titanic'']]
**An expedition to the [[shipwreck]] of the [[Titanic|RMS ''Titanic'']] reveals considerable deterioration of the bow, as well as the rediscovery of a bronze ''[[Diana of Versailles]]'' replica last seen during the initial survey of the wreck in 1986. [https://apnews.com/article/what-did-they-find-titanic-titan-sub-8158eb820dd1ab1a1407dc79f726c45c (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Pacific typhoon season]]
**At least 14 people are killed in [[landslide]]s and [[flood]]s caused by [[Tropical Storm Yagi (2024)|Tropical Storm Yagi]] in the [[Philippines]]. [https://apnews.com/article/tropical-storm-yagi-philippines-95604282315e6adade30a5a465a31562 (AP)]
*A bus veered off Van Rhyns Pass in the [[Western Cape]] and plunged down a mountain, killing 10 and injuring 29. [https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/van-rhyns-pass-bus-crash-death-toll-rises-to-10-while-29-farmworkers-still-in-hospital-20240903 (News 24)]
*A [[Chiva bus]] overturned in [[Huila Department]], [[Colombia]], killing eight and injuring dozens more. [https://colombiaone.com/2024/09/02/colombia-chiva-bus-dead/ (Colombia One)]
*An  Indian Coast Guard helicopter, carrying out a medical emergency flight, crashed in the [[Arabian Sea]] near [[Gujarat]], killing 3 of the four occupants.[https://www.news18.com/india/indian-coast-guard-helicopter-emergency-landing-gujarat-porbandar-crew-members-search-operation-9036949.html (NEWS18)]
* Three people are killed after their bus is struck by a mudslide in [[Kohistan District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-roadside-bomb-bus-passengers-dfd368d7ba03259ecb8356babbb706d5 (AP News)]
*A fire broke out in the Church of the [[Immaculate Conception]] in [[Saint-Omer]], [[France]].[https://www.catholic.org/news/international/europe/story.php?id=87219 (Catholic Online)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Ukraine]], [[Mongolia–Russia relations]]
**[[President of Russia]] [[Vladimir Putin]] arrives in [[Mongolia]] to discuss a [[China]]–[[Russia]] [[Pipeline|gas pipeline]] meant to recoup Russian losses from [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Western sanctions]], despite [[Ukraine]] and the [[European Union]] urging Mongolia to arrest Putin under his [[International Criminal Court]] warrant. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/putin-arrives-mongolia-key-link-planned-gas-pipeline-china-2024-09-02/ (Reuters)] [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2024/09/02/brussels-urges-mongolia-to-comply-with-icc-request-and-arrest-putin-during-official-visit (Euronews)]
**[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ukraine)|Ukraine's Foreign Ministry]] states that Mongolia's refusal to arrest Vladimir Putin while on a state visit means that it shares "responsibility for the war crimes" committed by Russia, and vows to work with allies to enforce punitive measures on Mongolia. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-criticises-mongolias-failure-arrest-putin-2024-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Foreign relations of Turkey]]
**[[Turkey]] formally applies to join the [[BRICS]] [[geopolitical]] bloc, citing the lack of progress in its [[Accession of Turkey to the European Union|accession]] to the [[European Union]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-09-02/turkey-submits-bid-to-join-brics-as-erdogan-pushes-for-new-alliances-beyond-west (Bloomberg)] [https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/diplomacy/turkiye-applies-for-brics-membership-in-push-for-new-alliances-report (''Daily Sabah'')]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**The [[United States]] seizes a [[Dassault Falcon 900]] [[Jet aircraft|jet]] used by [[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan president]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] on accusations that the purchase of the jet violated [[Sanctions during the Venezuelan crisis|U.S. sanctions against Venezuela]], and flies the jet from the [[Dominican Republic]] to [[Florida]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-seizes-venezuelan-presidents-plane-dominican-republic-2024-09-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Makala prison jailbreak attempt]]
**At least 129 inmates are killed and 59 more injured in an attempted [[Prison escape|prison break]] at {{ill|Makala Prison|fr|Centre pénitentiaire et de rééducation de Kinshasa}} in [[Kinshasa]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-prison-inmates-jailbreak-deaths-stampede-9322cf6fed04752172df6d57601eb51e (AP)]
*[[Brazilian investigation into Elon Musk]]
**The [[Brazil]]ian [[Supreme Federal Court|Supreme Court]] unanimously upholds justice [[Alexandre de Moraes]]' decision to block [[Social media|social media]] platform [[Twitter|X]], in the country. De Moraes also set a daily fine of [[Brazilian real|R$]]50,000 (US$8,900) for people or companies using [[VPN]]s to access the site. [https://apnews.com/article/brazil-musk-x-platform-moraes-shutdown-6942614705a4e85064f1d98628b49295 (AP)]
*[[Nth Room case]], [[Gender inequality in South Korea]]
**The [[South Korea]]n [[National Police Agency (South Korea)|National Police Agency]] announces an investigation into the messaging app [[Telegram (software)|Telegram]] for abetting and hosting [[chat room]]s that distribute [[deepfake pornography]], including of [[child pornography|children]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-launches-telegram-deepfake-porn-probe/a-70107568 (DW)]
*[[2024 CTA shooting]]
**Four people are killed in a [[mass shooting]] targeting [[Homelessness in the United States|homeless]] people on a [[Chicago Transit Authority]] [[train]] in [[Forest Park, Illinois|Forest Park]], [[Illinois]], [[United States]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/chicago/news/shots-fired-at-chicago-areas-forest-park-blue-line/#site-header:26 (WBBM-TV)]
*One person is fatally shot and at least four other people are injured including one person who was critically injured in a [[mass shooting]] at the [[West Indian Day Parade]] in [[Brooklyn]], New York, United States. [https://apnews.com/article/new-york-west-indian-caribbean-parade-carnival-b2b87995006cfd8ab598862599905c52 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**[[Israel–Hamas war protests in the United States]]
***Thousands of people gather in [[Manhattan]], [[New York City]], United States, to protest against the [[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]], rally for support of [[Palestinians]], and call for New York institutions to [[divest]] from Israeli businesses. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/newyork/news/nyc-protest-support-for-gaza-union-square/ (CBS News)]
**[[September 2024 Israel ceasefire protests]]
***[[Histadrut]], [[Israel]]'s [[national trade union center]], begins a one-day [[general strike]] to protest against the [[Thirty-seventh government of Israel|Netanyahu government]]'s failure to [[negotiate]] a [[Three-phase Israel–Hamas war ceasefire proposal|ceasefire]] and [[Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis|hostage]] deal. The strike is later [[Court order|ordered]] to end prematurely by a [[Tel Aviv]] labor court, claiming the strike was illegally political in nature rather than economic. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgez7ez10lo (BBC)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/sep/02/israel-gaza-war-national-strike-hostages-ceasefire-netanyahu (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Didier Guillaume]] is sworn in as the new [[Minister of State (Monaco)|Minister of State of Monaco]], the principality's head of government, succeeding [[Pierre Dartout]]. [https://www.palais.mc/en/news/h-s-h-prince-albert-ii/event/2024/september/swearing-in-of-h-e-mr-didier-guillaume-minister-of-state-3566.html (Royal Palace)]
